title: Learning Interaction Pattern Library
principle: Idea bank, not a lesson template and not a component catalog. Use only after lesson architecture and learning moments are defined. Describe the ideal interaction first, then use this library to widen the option space; inspect the component registry only afterwards.
rules: Do not select a pattern merely because it exists.
Do not use this library to invent the lesson architecture; architecture must already be selected.
Describe the ideal interaction and required mechanics before checking existing components.
Tags describe pedagogical role; they do not prescribe the internal interaction.
A pattern may use an existing component, an adapted component, a composition, a generic renderer, or a new component.
Reuse is preferred only when it preserves the core learning mechanic. Never downgrade a simulation, construction, exploration or stateful interaction merely to fit an existing component.
If the selected mechanic requires a new component, implementing that component is part of the lesson task.
Do not repeat the same pedagogical recipe in consecutive learning moments without a clear reason.
Do not place a light check immediately after text that already gives the complete answer the check asks the learner to reproduce.
LIGHT interactions are useful for recall and checking, but a lesson must not consist only of LIGHT major interactions when the content supports deeper digital learning.
MEDIUM and HEAVY interactions may carry new learning content; do not pre-explain all of their discoveries in text.
Consider a persistent learning object or evolving state when several moments can naturally operate on the same model, artifact, system, case or dataset.
'Бързи 5 въпроса' may use different response mechanics when pedagogically useful; variety itself is not a goal.
Exercise tasks may include agent-generated DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, CSV, ZIP, images, datasets or starter files.
Sandbox should permit safe experimentation with visible consequences or state changes.
For visualizations, choose the simplest form that preserves the intended cognitive action and learning mechanic - not merely the simplest available component.
Game framing is optional and must serve a learning action.
A fancy title or story wrapper does not make a familiar mechanic new.

quick_checks.risk: Easy to turn into text-to-check duplication. Do not use as the dominant learning engine.

matching_classification.risk: Becomes trivial when the mapping or categories were just stated explicitly.

ordering.risk: Fails when the preceding text already lists the exact order.

visualization.risk: A clickable reveal is not automatically meaningful interaction. Prefer exploration, comparison or manipulation when the concept needs it.

games.risk: Do not mistake game framing for cognitive depth. A quiz in a game skin remains a light check.

scenarios.risk: Do not reduce a branching or consequence-driven scenario to static multiple choice.

sandbox.risk: If the learner cannot change state or observe consequences, it is probably not a real sandbox.

authentic_tasks.risk: Do not replace authentic file work with a description of what the learner would have done.

discussion_reflection.risk: Do not append automatically at the end; place where the decision or reflection is actually needed.

media_story.risk: Narrative continuity alone is not learning continuity. The learner's action/state must also carry the throughline.

precondition: Lesson architecture has already been selected.
Major learning moments have already been defined.
steps: State the learner action and the new understanding required.
Describe the ideal interaction without considering the component registry.
List the mechanics required by that ideal interaction.
Use this library to shortlist several patterns or pattern combinations.
Reject patterns that would reduce discovery, construction, simulation, state change or consequence to simple recall.
Choose the pattern or composition that best preserves the intended cognitive action.
Only now inspect the component registry.
Reuse only if the existing component preserves the core mechanic; otherwise adapt, compose or build a new component.
hard_fail_conditions: All major interactions in the lesson are LIGHT.
The preceding text already contains the complete answer required by the interaction.
A stateful/simulation/construction design is replaced with a simpler existing component solely for implementation convenience.
Several consecutive learning moments repeat the same exposition-then-check recipe.
A pattern is chosen mainly because it already exists as a component.
A fancy title or game/story skin is used to claim novelty without changing the learning mechanic.

weight_guidance.LIGHT: Recall, recognition or short verification of knowledge already available to the learner.
weight_guidance.MEDIUM: Application, comparison, diagnosis, decision or reorganization in a meaningfully new case.
weight_guidance.HEAVY: The interaction/environment itself carries substantial new learning through construction, manipulation, exploration, changing state or consequences.
important: Weight is contextual, not immutable. A matching task can become MEDIUM if it requires inference from novel evidence; a game can remain LIGHT if it only skins recall questions.
Do not pre-explain all discoveries of a MEDIUM or HEAVY interaction in the text immediately above it.
The goal is not to maximize HEAVY interactions. The goal is to use enough depth for the learning objective while keeping the lesson moderate.

profile_note: Pattern profiles are defaults for ideation, not fixed truth. The same pattern can change weight depending on prior information, task novelty, feedback, state and learner action. The lesson plan must assign the final contextual weight.
